summary: Verified Kingdom Notes browser flow end-to-end. Landing, sign-up, and login all work; login for confirmed test account authenticates via Supabase and navigates to /game/onboarding. Onboarding character creation succeeds (POST /rest/v1/characters -> 201) and /game renders the full character dashboard for the newly-created TestMinister. Client-side @supabase/ssr session cookie is set correctly (single chunk, 2627 chars, name 'sb-dwmvbowpdhfktkbwpzys-auth-token'). CRITICAL infrastructure issue: every /api/game/* route returns 502 Bad Gateway through the public preview URL because the Kubernetes ingress routes /api/* to port 8001 (FastAPI backend slot) while this Next.js-only app serves /api/* itself from port 3000. On localhost:3000 the same Next.js API routes respond correctly (200 for public /api/game/lodgings, 401 for /api/game/challenges without auth), so the server-side auth path could NOT be verified via the public URL. Server-cookie SSR parsing is thus unverified end-to-end from the browser.

critical.issue: All Next.js API routes return 502 Bad Gateway via preview.emergentagent.com ingress. K8s ingress routes /api/* to port 8001 where the FastAPI supervisor is FATAL (no /app/backend directory exists — this is a Next.js-only app). Same routes work on localhost:3000 (200/401 as expected). Blocks in-app calls: /api/game/lodgings, /api/game/presence, /api/game/challenges, /api/game/opportunities all fail from the browser.

minor.issue: Supabase returns 406 when character row does not yet exist (PostgREST .single() with no rows). Handled gracefully by client but noisy in console.

integration_issues.issue: 502 from /api/game/* through public URL — data panels will silently render empty on the deployed preview environment. Not a code bug; ingress rewrite issue.

issues: Vercel Web Analytics script 404 (/_vercel/insights/script.js) — harmless but pollutes console. Consider removing @vercel/analytics or gating on VERCEL env.

action_items: INFRA/ENV: Ingress is routing /api/* to port 8001 but no server runs there. For a Next.js-only app the ingress must route /api/* to the Next.js server on :3000, OR the platform config must allow the app to serve /api/* from port 3000. Recommend either (a) reconfiguring the ingress rule for this preview environment, or (b) running a tiny reverse proxy on :8001 that forwards to :3000 (e.g. socat/nginx) so external /api/* traffic reaches Next.js.

Because of the 502, the SSR cookie parsing in lib/supabase/server.ts (chunked/base64 @supabase/ssr cookie handling — the originally flagged potential bug) COULD NOT be verified from the browser. On localhost:3000, /api/game/challenges returned 401 without auth (expected). Recommend main agent to (i) fix the ingress, then (ii) rerun this test to confirm /api/game/challenges returns 200 when the browser sends the sb-<ref>-auth-token cookie. If it still returns 401 after ingress fix, THEN the server.ts cookie parser needs updating.
Consider removing the Vercel Analytics script (or conditional-loading it) to silence the 404s.
critical_code_review_comments: lib/supabase/server.ts manually JSON.parses the auth cookie and picks parsed.access_token || parsed[0]. Modern @supabase/ssr cookies can be base64-prefixed ('base64-<payload>') and/or chunked ('<name>.0', '<name>.1'). Current parser handles neither. Recommend switching to createServerClient from @supabase/ssr with cookies() from next/headers instead of hand-rolling the parse. (Not verifiable end-to-end here due to ingress 502.)

app/auth/login/page.tsx uses only router.push('/game') after signIn; no router.refresh(). With App Router + @supabase/ssr, a router.refresh() after signInWithPassword ensures Server Components see the new session. Current behaviour still worked in this test because the middleware/getUser refetches on the /game render, but it's fragile.

If 401 -> server.ts cookie parsing is broken; if 502 -> ingress still misrouted.
rca of the issue: Root cause of /api/game/* 502: this preview environment's K8s ingress rewrites all /api/* paths to backend port 8001 (standard FastAPI+React template assumption), but the app is a pure Next.js app that owns /api/*. The supervisor 'backend' program is FATAL because /app/backend does not exist. Localhost:3000/api/game/* works (verified via curl: 200 on /api/game/lodgings, 401 on /api/game/challenges without auth). Mitigation options: reconfigure ingress for Next.js apps, or run a lightweight :8001 -> :3000 proxy via supervisor.
